audit_2026_10_18: Source audit (live Socrata API, 2026-10-18): dataset uhjb-xac9 'Cincinnati Building Permits' on data.cincinnati-oh.gov, publisher City of Cincinnati (Buildings & Inspections data entered by that department; portal owner Office of Performance & Data Analytics), license Public Domain, portal-stated refresh frequency Daily. IMPORTANT — the dataset was REPLACED by a new extract on 2026-10-18T12:05:30Z (rowsUpdatedAt): the first audit reads (~15:47Z) still saw the pre-replacement extract (466,282 rows, text-valued status/class fields, permitnum unique) on a lagging read path; every subsequent measurement agrees on the post-replacement extract and it was probed stable (181,172 rows all-time, applied range 2010-01-04 to 2026-10-16). ALL build measurements below are on the post-replacement extract; gate 4's pre-pull baseline protects every future run the same way if the source flips again. Post-replacement shape: 31 columns, codes instead of text (statuscurrentmapped labels, permitclass = RCO/OBC building-code class), some text values wrapped in literal double quotes (CSV-import artifact, stripped at normalization), and a COMPONENT grain (see dedupe_rule). Trailing-12-month issue window (issueddate >= 2025-10-17): 10,417 rows = 9,788 distinct permitnum; rows are exactly unique per (permitnum, description) pair (10,417 pairs); the 609 multi-row permits' rows disagree on NONE of issueddate, applieddate, originaladdress1, originalzip, jurisdiction, permitclass, statuscurrentmapped, companyname, workclassmapped, or pin. Window jurisdiction is uniformly CINCINNATI and originalcity is CINCINNATI (one null-city row) — a city feed. Window statuses (statuscurrentmapped): Permit Issued 6,260 / Permit Finaled 4,116 / Permit Withdrawn 24 / Approved 5 / small residue of process codes. permitclass is published on 100% of window rows: RCO 5,903 / OBC 4,514. NO electrical signal exists anywhere in the feed (zero window rows mention electrical work in description, permittypemapped, or permittype) — the dataset carries no electrical permits. The dataset publishes no applicant/owner person-name fields at all (31-column schema verified). VALUATION (estprojectcostdec, a TEXT column): 100% present and parseable on window rows; row level 674 zeros / 4 at $1 / 9,738 above $1. At permit level (component sums, see field_map.valuation) the window total is $1,240,768,378.84 across 9,788 permits; 278 permits total $0 and 4 total $1 (2.9% of permits at $1 or less; contrast Austin's ~80%-of-valued-at-$1). The most-repeated permit totals above $1M are round applicant budgets ($1,500,000 x7, $2,100,000 x4) — the signature of round declared estimates, not a system stamp (contrast Seattle's identical non-round $24,102,600 stamped across 38 unrelated demolition permits; no such pattern exists here). The largest permit ($140,000,000, a single New Building component at 444 Plum St, Skanska USA Building Inc) appears exactly once and is 11.28% of the window total. A theoretical double-count signature (largest component exactly equal to the sum of a permit's other components — mostly two-equal-component permits) bounds any overstatement at 1.35% of the total. September 2026 source aggregates (permit grain): 828 rows = 763 permits, $115,264,789.61 (cross-check targets). Freshest issueddate in the table: 2026-10-16.
coverage_note: City of Cincinnati permits only (Hamilton County page scope). County-wide coverage is NOT implied. The city's dataset carries no electrical permits.

dedupe_rule.definition: A 'permit' for Cincinnati = one permitnum issued by the City of Cincinnati Buildings & Inspections Department. The feed's grain (post-2026-10-18 extract) is one row per work COMPONENT a permit covers: a permit that covers excavation plus a new building appears as two rows sharing one permitnum, one application date, one issue date, one address, and one company of record, differing in the component label (description), the component's mapped type, and the component's own estimated cost, square footage, and units. The pipeline collapses each permit's component rows into one record (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the record's trade is classified from the component set, and its value is the sum of the components' stated costs.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issueddate >= 2025-10-17), measured 2026-10-18 against the live API on the post-replacement extract: 10,417 rows vs 9,788 distinct permitnum (9,179 permits with 1 component row, 589 with 2, 20 with 3); rows are exactly unique per (permitnum, description) — 10,417 pairs. Across all 609 multi-row permits, the rows disagree on NONE of issueddate, applieddate, originaladdress1, originalzip, jurisdiction, permitclass, statuscurrentmapped, companyname, workclassmapped, or pin (measured on a full-window pull, and re-asserted by the pipeline's collapse step on the production pull).
dedupe_rule.rule: source_record_id = permitnum. Collapse happens in the pipeline (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the in-batch duplicate gate and the DB upsert key remain as guards.

field_map.category: permitclass — the building code the permit was issued under, published on 100% of window rows: RCO (Residential Code of Ohio) -> residential (5,903 window rows), OBC (Ohio Building Code) -> commercial (4,514 window rows)
field_map.contractor_rule: companyname ONLY — the permit's published company of record (present on 10,305 of 10,417 window rows; 1,848 distinct values; the dataset publishes no applicant/owner person-name fields at all, verified against the full 31-column schema 2026-10-18). The extract wraps some values in literal double quotes (CSV artifact) — stripped at normalization. The city's 'OWNER' value (175 window rows) is its code for owner-permitted work and names no company: carried as NULL, never as a contractor name.
field_map.locality: originalcity (CINCINNATI on all but one window row; the issuing jurisdiction is the default when blank)
field_map.permit_type_source: permittypemapped of the permit's components, joined (the component's own mapped type names the trade family directly: Building, Plumbing Permits, HVAC, Fire Protection Systems, ...)
field_map.project_description: the permit's component labels (the source's `description` field IS the component label — the dataset publishes no free-text scope of work; proposeduse is a code and is not published as prose)
field_map.source_record_id: permitnum (one published permit = one permit number; its component rows collapse — see dedupe_rule)
field_map.status_source: statuscurrentmapped (falls back to statuscurrent); mapped via registry status_map
field_map.valuation: estprojectcostdec (a TEXT column) — SUM of the permit's component costs: each component row states its own slice of the permit's estimated project cost (e.g. permit 2025P09293: HVAC component $6,037,000 + New Building component $77,550,000 = $83,587,000), so the permit's reported value is the sum of its components, counted once per permit. Validated 2026-10-18 (see audit): 100% of window rows carry a parseable figure; 97.1% of permits total more than $1; no placeholder or sibling-stamp pathology (the most-repeated large totals are round applicant budgets); the theoretical worst-case double-count signature bounds overstatement at 1.35% of the window total; the DB window sum must reproduce the independently computed $1,240,768,378.84. Values are applicants' stated estimates, printed as reported (SOP rule 2).
field_map.work_type_source: the permit's component labels (description) — dedicated classifier pass: trades.classify_cincinnati_trade
